react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network activity scoring — converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbed androgen and estrogen steroid hormone metabolism. RaMP ORA reports the pathway with FDR 2.9×10⁻¹⁵ across five simultaneous database hits (SMPDB SMP00068, KEGG map00150, Reactome R-HSA-196071, WikiPathways WP496, WP2263). MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently recovers KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as the sole significant hit at p = 4.36×10⁻⁷ using only the five steroid input compounds. Mummichog reports the matched KEGG-derived network module 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' as its top-ranked pathway (p = 8.4×10⁻⁵) with 11 of 11 module members hit, including all five input steroids plus six network-proximal neighbours. The five driver metabolites — estrone (KEGG:C00468), dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), estradiol (KEGG:C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917) — represent a substrate-to-product continuum in the steroidogenic axis: DHEA serves as the C19 precursor, testosterone as the central C19 intermediate, DHT as the potent 5α-reduced androgen product, and estrone/estradiol as the aromatized C18 estrogen arm. Guanidinoacetic acid (KEGG:C00581) independently maps to the urea cycle / glycine-serine-threonine metabolism branch (Mummichog rank 6, p = 0.047), consistent with creatine-biosynthesis linkage. N-acetylgalactosamine (CHEBI:28800) resolved from its InChIKey OVRNDRQMDRJTHS but falls outside the steroid cluster, appearing only in peripheral amino-sugar pathways at the noise boundary. The unanimous cross-paradigm verdict is a coordinated dysregulation of the androgen–estrogen biosynthetic axis, with aromatase (CYP19A1, catalyzing testosterone→estrone) and 17β-HSD (catalyzing estrone↔estradiol interconversion) as the key enzyme nodes.
